ticket: JSRT-18 interp.rs split (required first commit) + Annex B.3.3 block-function hoisting + generator/annexB re-triage

items.item: Split interp.rs's statement-execution/disposal machinery into interp_stmt.rs
items.root_cause: interp.rs was 4,234 lines (over AGENTS.md's 4,000-line-per-file limit), up from 3,990 before JSRT-17's using/await-using disposal machinery landed in it.
items.fix: Pure code motion, no behavior change: moved the Disposable struct, stmt_declares_resource, for_of_dispose_kind, and the entire contiguous exec_stmt/exec_stmts impl-Interpreter method sequence (loops, try/catch/for-of, job draining, dispose_method/add_disposable/dispose_frame/await_value) into a new interp_stmt.rs, spliced back in via the existing include! convention (matches this codebase's flat-module include! pattern -- item visibility/order doesn't matter across included files). interp.rs dropped from 4,234 to 1,587 lines; interp_stmt.rs is 2,660. Verified zero behavior change via amazing-js crate tests (406 pass, 1 skip, identical to pre-split) and --doc (1 passed).

items.item: Annex B.3.3 block-level function-declaration web-compat hoisting
items.root_cause: This mechanism did not exist at all. The pre-existing top-level hoist() pass recursed into every nested block/if/loop body and, for ANY FunctionDeclaration found there, eagerly bound it to its function value directly in the outer function/script/global scope -- unconditionally, regardless of strict mode, and evaluated too early (at hoist time, not at block-evaluation time). This meant: (a) strict-mode block-scoped functions incorrectly leaked into the enclosing scope (should ReferenceError there instead); (b) sloppy-mode block-scoped functions were visible in the outer scope with the function VALUE before the block ever ran (should be `undefined` until the block's FunctionDeclaration statement is actually evaluated); (c) there was no real per-block lexical binding for the function at all -- it only appeared to work because of the same over-eager outer leak. Caused the bulk of annexB's ~580 file failures (dominant clusters: 'An initialized binding is not created prior/following evaluation Expected a ReferenceError...', 'Expected SameValue(function, undefined)'/'(outer declaration, inner declaration)', 'identifier already declared', 'f is not defined').
items.fix: Adapted from lucid-softworks/lumen (crates/lumen/src/interpreter.rs collect_annexb_funcs/HoistOp::AnnexB, crates/lumen/src/eval.rs annexb_fn_sync_eval) @ f6c9860d44fa52249cfd647122edea184d32c863, MIT, onto this codebase's Result<Flow,Throw> tree-walker and its EnvHandle/BindingCell model (rather than lumen's own scope-graph). Three parts: (1) hoist() split into a nested-aware hoist_inner(body, env, nested, blocked): the direct top-level statement list of a function/script/module/eval body keeps the old eager unconditional bind (nested=false); recursing into Block/If/While/DoWhile/For/ForIn/ForOf/ForAwaitOf/Labeled sets nested=true, where a plain (non-async, non-generator) FunctionDeclaration only gets an undefined-initialized legacy var binding (env.hoist_var, idempotent) when !strict_eval_context and its name isn't shadowed by an intervening let/const/class/using/await-using declaration -- tracked via a blocked: Vec<String> threaded through recursion (block_lexical_names + push_blocked, new free fns in interp_stmt.rs). StmtKind::Try's own recursive arm deliberately still starts a *fresh* hoist() (nested=false) -- Annex B promotion out of try/catch/finally bodies is an explicit, documented known gap, left untouched to avoid risking that area's existing behavior. (2) StmtKind::Block's execution gained a block-entry pre-pass (BlockDeclarationInstantiation's own function-hoisting, independent of Annex B, strict mode included): every direct FunctionDeclaration child gets a fresh closure lexically bound into the block's own new env at every entry to the block. (3) StmtKind::Function's exec_stmt arm (previously a pure no-op) became the Annex B sync step: in sloppy mode, for a plain function, walk to env.var_scope() and, only if it already holds a non-lexical cell for that name (BindingCell::is_lexical(), new pub method on env.rs), copy the block's own current value into it via scope.assign() (not a raw cell write -- Env::resolve_raw/assign_raw special-case Global-kind scopes to read/write through the global OBJECT's property rather than the cell's own .value, which a first attempt using a raw BindingCell::set() missed, caught by a regression in the global-code/eval-code annexB subset before the fix).

known_gaps: Annex B.3.3 promotion out of try/catch/finally block bodies is unimplemented (hoist()'s Try arm deliberately still does the old eager/unconditional bind, unchanged from before this ticket, to avoid risk to that area).

Annex B.3.4 (a bare, brace-less `if (x) function f(){}` / `if (x) f(); else function f(){}` position, with no enclosing Block) is unimplemented: the sync step depends on a Block's block-entry pre-pass having already lexically bound the name locally, which a brace-less position never gets. hoist_inner still correctly reserves the outer var placeholder for this position, but it never gets synced away from undefined.

Annex B's legacy RegExp static accessors (RegExp.$1-$9, input, lastMatch, lastParen, leftContext, rightContext, and their prototype/constructor property descriptors) do not exist at all -- a second, unrelated annexB cluster (~20+ residual failures under annexB/built-ins/RegExp/legacy-accessors), confirmed by inspection to be a completely separate feature from the block-function-hoisting fix above.

NamedEvaluation (IsAnonymousFunctionDefinition -> SetFunctionName) is not implemented for ANY binding form in this interpreter -- confirmed by direct probe that plain `let fn = function(){}; fn.name` already yields '' (not 'fn') with no using/await-using involved at all. This is why using/await-using's 'fn-name-{arrow,cls,cover,fn,gen}.js' tests fail (10 across using, 10 across await-using): they are a symptom of this pre-existing, cross-the-board gap (affects var/let/const/using/await-using identically), not a using/await-using-specific defect, and a narrow using-only patch would be inconsistent. Left as an out-of-scope, separately-ticketable gap rather than attempting a partial fix.

GeneratorFunction/AsyncGeneratorFunction residuals re-triaged per this ticket's explicit request: re-checked whether any of the 'value is not callable' failures (14 in AsyncGeneratorFunction, 4 in GeneratorFunction) were something OTHER than the long-standing js-vm generator-execution blocker. Root-caused built-ins/GeneratorFunction/invoked-as-function-no-arguments.js and its siblings: GeneratorFunction()-constructed generator functions (CreateDynamicFunction path) still hit the same underlying gap as `function*(){}` literals when called -- just via a different code path that returns a value without a working .next(), rather than the clean 'generators are not implemented' TypeError literal-syntax generators raise. Confirmed same root cause, no quick fix available without js-vm; left as-is.

await_value's lack of true suspension (pending promises degrade to undefined) and await-using disposal at async-function/async-generator-body exit (needs a vm/ hook) are unchanged from JSRT-17 and still open; see js-runtime_jsrt17_evidence.json and questions.md.

gates.crate_amazing_js: 406 pass, 1 skip (cargo nextest -p amazing-js --locked) -- both before and after the interp.rs/interp_stmt.rs split, proving zero behavior change from the split itself.

test262_before_after.note: Directory-scoped scripts/test262.py --only runs, before (base_sha 8cb72625, i.e. dev tip after JSRT-17's merge) vs after (this ticket's implementation), in one linux-run on venus-003, per the coordinator's JSRT-18 gate (no full Boat sweep; the integrator runs that at merge).

language/statements/using.after: 68 pass / 12 fail (unchanged; fn-name cluster diagnosed as a pre-existing cross-the-board NamedEvaluation gap, not using-specific -- see known_gaps)

language/statements/await-using.after: 47 pass / 45 fail / 6 unsupported (unchanged; same NamedEvaluation diagnosis)

test262_before_after.result: annexB gains +105 passing files (471 -> 576), zero losses. Every other anchor directory holds its exact JSRT-17 count -- zero losses, zero unintended regressions from the interp.rs split or the Annex B change.

gates.workspace_nextest: 3381 pass, 0 fail, 17 skip, 120.868s (cargo nextest run --workspace --locked) -- identical counts to JSRT-17's own workspace gate, confirming zero regressions from either the interp.rs split or the Annex B change.
